title: Resource suppression and polite web behaviour
summary: Virtual Browser must understand why resources are requested so it can suppress irrelevant browser traffic and police application polling before API Client performs network admission.
invariants: HTML, JavaScript and application data may be fetched when required for semantics.
Images, fonts, media, analytics and advertising are not fetched merely because markup references them.
Application polling intervals may be clamped to policy minimums instead of blindly reproducing consumer-browser cadence.
Browser resource policy may be stricter than API Client policy but must never weaken API Client route/rate/security policy.
Page-level budgets and per-origin request limits are legitimate browser policy even when API Client has spare capacity.

provenance.claim: API Client bounds transport and leaves higher-level request semantics to callers.
Virtual Browser remains authoritative for browser semantics while API Client remains authoritative for outbound traffic.
